chunks.title: Welcome: Every child is known, heard and challenged
chunks.text:
Every child is known, heard and challenged
At Indigo Academy West, girls and boys learn side by side in small classes where the teacher has time for every pupil. We believe children learn best when they feel safe, are curious, and are asked to think rather than just to remember.
Our primary school combines the Russian-language programme with the Singapore method of teaching. From Grade 7 our pupils move to the Cambridge programme, and all along the way English is part of every day.
Director, Indigo Academy West
Read the Director’s welcome

chunks.title: Why Indigo West: What makes our school different
chunks.text:
More English — More English lessons than in most schools, with native-speaking teachers on our staff. Children practise English every day, not only in class.
Singapore method — Primary teachers use the Singapore approach: from objects to pictures to abstract ideas, so pupils truly understand, not just memorise.
More than lessons — Robotics, chess, komuz and other extra subjects are part of the timetable, not an optional extra after school.
One-to-one attention — Like every Indigo Academy school, we follow each pupil individually: their pace, their strengths and what they need next.

chunks.text:

chunks.title: Our story: An Indigo school for the west of Bishkek
chunks.text:
An Indigo school for the west of Bishkek
Indigo Academy West belongs to Indigo Academy, a network of private schools in Bishkek known for its strong teaching and close attention to every child.
Families asked for a school that combines a solid academic base with modern methods, real English practice and a broader education. Indigo Academy West is our answer: a co-educational school for Grades 1–12, with the Singapore method in primary school and the Cambridge programme from Grade 7.

chunks.title: Our mission
chunks.text: To educate curious, well-mannered and confident young people who think independently, speak several languages and are ready for the world.

chunks.title: Our vision
chunks.text: To be the school families in Bishkek choose when they want a strong education, real English and international opportunities for their children.

chunks.title: Our values: Five words we live by
chunks.text:
Respect — for teachers, for classmates and for every person.
Curiosity — to ask questions and to look for answers.
Responsibility — for our learning, our words and our school.
Kindness — shown in small everyday actions.
Openness — to new languages, cultures and ideas.

chunks.title: Director’s welcome: Dear parents and guests
chunks.text:
Dear parents and guests
Thank you for your interest in Indigo Academy West. Choosing a school is one of the most important decisions a family makes, and we are honoured that you are considering us.
Our teachers know every child by name. They notice when a pupil is ready for a bigger challenge and when they need a little more support. We measure success not only in grades, but in how confidently our pupils think, speak and work with others, in their own language and in English.
I warmly invite you to visit us, to see our lessons and to talk with our team.
Director, Indigo Academy West

chunks.title: Our approach: Why families choose us
chunks.text:
Individual attention — Small classes and teachers who follow each pupil’s progress closely.
Real English — More hours of English and native-speaking teachers on our staff.
A broader education — Robotics, chess and komuz as subjects, building logic, creativity and culture.
An international path — The Cambridge programme from Grade 7 and preparation for universities abroad.

chunks.title: Primary School
chunks.text:
Grades 1–6
Russian-language classes taught with the Singapore method, more English than in most schools, and robotics, chess and komuz in the weekly timetable.

chunks.title: How we teach: Strong foundations, taught the modern way
chunks.text:
Russian-language programme — Primary classes follow the Russian-language programme, giving children a solid base in reading, writing and mathematics.
Singapore method — Our teachers are trained in the Singapore approach: pupils discuss, work in pairs and explain their thinking.
More English — Extra English lessons every week so children start speaking early and naturally.
Small classes — Teachers have time for each child, their questions and their pace.

chunks.title: Singapore method: Understanding first, then speed
chunks.text:
Understanding first, then speed
The Singapore method, used by schools around the world, teaches children to understand an idea before they memorise rules. Pupils move through three steps:
Concrete
Children touch and move real objects: blocks, counters, cards.
Pictorial
They draw what they did, using models such as the famous “bar model”.
Abstract
Only then do they write numbers and symbols, now with real understanding.

chunks.title: In the timetable: Robotics, chess and komuz are lessons here
chunks.text:
Unlike other private schools, these subjects are part of the weekly timetable for every primary pupil, alongside further clubs after lessons.
Robotics — Building and programming robots: engineering thinking from the first grades.
Chess — Logic, focus and planning, and learning to win and lose with dignity.
Komuz — Playing the national instrument: rhythm, memory and love for Kyrgyz culture.
Extra clubs — Art, sport, English speaking club and more, so every child finds their thing.

chunks.text:
More English, from Grade 1
Our primary pupils have more English lessons than in most schools. The aim is practice: children listen, speak, sing, read and play in English every week, with our English teachers and native English-speaking teachers.

Grades 7–12
From Grade 7 our pupils study in the Cambridge programme, with individual attention, strong English and preparation for universities and competitions around the world.

chunks.title: Our approach: Cambridge standards, Indigo care
chunks.text:
Cambridge programme — An internationally recognised curriculum that teaches pupils to think, analyse and apply knowledge.
One-to-one attention — As in all Indigo Academy schools, every pupil’s progress is followed individually.
Strong English — English is developed to an academic level, with native English-speaking teachers on staff.
Ready for the world — Preparation for international exams, competitions and studying abroad.

chunks.title: Cambridge pathway: Step by step to Grade 12
chunks.text:
The Cambridge programme builds knowledge and skills year after year, from the first secondary grades to graduation.
Grades 7–8 — Foundations — Pupils adapt to the Cambridge programme and to learning across subjects in English. — Cambridge Lower Secondary subjects — Study and research skills — Academic English
Grades 9–10 — Deeper study — Subjects become more demanding and pupils start to choose their focus. — Mathematics, sciences and English in depth — Projects and presentations — Olympiads and competitions
Grades 11–12 — Ready for university — Focused preparation for international examinations and university admission. — International examinations — IELTS and university preparation — Career and university guidance

chunks.title: One-to-one attention: Every pupil has a plan
chunks.text:
Every pupil has a plan
Teenagers need both challenge and support. Our teachers know each pupil well: their strengths, their gaps and their goals.
Progress is reviewed regularly, extra support is offered where it is needed, and pupils who are ready for more are given more. Parents always know how their child is doing.

chunks.title: The international stage: Preparing for the world
chunks.text:
Our pupils are prepared not only for exams, but for studying, competing and working with people from other countries.
International exams — Cambridge examinations and IELTS preparation.
Olympiads & competitions — Subject olympiads and international competitions.
Debate & public speaking — Presenting, arguing and leading in English.
University abroad — Guidance on choosing and applying to universities around the world.

chunks.title: Admissions
chunks.text: We are glad that you are considering Indigo Academy West for your child. Our admissions team will guide you through every step.

chunks.title: Step by step: How to join us
chunks.text:
Get in touch — Call or message us on WhatsApp to ask about places in your child’s grade.
Visit the school — Tour the building, see lessons and meet the admissions team.
Meet and assess — A friendly conversation for future first graders. From Grade 2, a short assessment in mathematics and English.
Submit documents — Bring the documents from the list below to the school office.
Welcome to Indigo West — Sign the agreement, receive the uniform information and get ready for the first day.

chunks.title: Documents: What to prepare
chunks.text:
Copy of the birth certificate
Copies of both parents’ passports
Medical record (form 026/u) and vaccination card
Personal file and report card from the previous school (for transfers)
3×4 cm photographs, 4 pieces
Application form completed at the school office

chunks.title: Tuition fees
chunks.text: Tuition is set for each academic year. Please contact the admissions office for current fees and payment options.

chunks.title: Which grades do you teach?
chunks.text: We teach Grades 1–12. Primary school is Grades 1–6; middle and high school, with the Cambridge programme, is Grades 7–12.

chunks.title: Is the school for boys and girls?
chunks.text: Yes. Indigo Academy West is a co-educational school: boys and girls study together.

chunks.title: In which language are primary classes taught?
chunks.text: Primary classes follow the Russian-language programme, with extra English lessons every week and Kyrgyz language lessons.

chunks.title: What is the Singapore method?
chunks.text: A way of teaching, especially mathematics, in which children first work with objects, then with pictures and models, and only then with numbers and symbols. It builds real understanding.

chunks.title: Are robotics, chess and komuz paid extras?
chunks.text: No, at Indigo Academy West robotics, chess and komuz are part of the timetable. Please ask the office about any additional clubs.

chunks.title: Do you have native English-speaking teachers?
chunks.text: Yes. Native English-speaking teachers are part of our teaching staff.

chunks.title: Can we visit before applying?
chunks.text: Yes, and we recommend it. Call us to agree a convenient day and time for a personal tour.

chunks.title: School Life
chunks.text: School is more than lessons. It is friendship, projects, competitions, celebrations and the feeling of belonging.

chunks.title: A typical day: A day at Indigo West
chunks.text:
08:00 — Morning welcome — Pupils are met at the door by their teachers.
08:30 — Lessons begin — Core subjects while minds are fresh.
12:30 — Lunch and rest — Time to eat together and talk with friends.
14:00 — Robotics, chess, komuz, clubs — Signature subjects, clubs, sport and supervised homework.
17:00 — Home time — Parents collect their children from school.

chunks.title: Subjects & clubs: Find what you love
chunks.text:

Robotics

chunks.title: Traditions: Moments we celebrate together
chunks.text:
Knowledge Day — The first bell of the school year on 1 September.
Teachers’ Day — Concerts and gratitude for our teachers.
English Week — Performances, quizzes and projects in English.
New Year concert — Performances, decorations and family guests.
Nooruz — Sumolok, national costumes, komuz and spring celebrations on 21 March.
Last Bell & graduation — Farewell to our graduates at the end of the year.

chunks.title: Wellbeing: Care for every child
chunks.text:
Class teacher — A trusted adult who follows each pupil’s progress and wellbeing.
School psychologist — Support with emotions, friendships and exam stress.
Medical office — A nurse on site during the school day.
Partnership with parents — Regular meetings and open communication with families.

chunks.title: Our Team
chunks.text: Our teachers are the heart of the school: experienced professionals, specialist teachers and native English speakers who care about every child.

chunks.title: Join our team
chunks.text: We are always glad to meet talented teachers, including native English speakers, who share our values. Send your CV to our office via WhatsApp.

chunks.title: News & Events
chunks.text: The latest news, photos and announcements appear first on our Instagram. Here is the calendar of our main school-year events.

Grades 7–8 — Foundations — Pupils adapt to the Cambridge programme and to learning across subjects in English. — Cambridge Lower Secondary subjects — Study and research skills — Academic English
Grades 9–10 — Deeper study — Subjects become more demanding and pupils start to choose their focus. — Mathematics, sciences and English in depth — Projects and presentations — Olympiads and competitions
Grades 11–12 — Ready for university — Focused preparation for international examinations and university admission. — International examinations — IELTS and university preparation — Career and university guidance

## Admissions (admissions.html)
We are glad that you are considering Indigo Academy West for your child. Our admissions team will guide you through every step.

## Step by step: How to join us (admissions.html)
Get in touch — Call or message us on WhatsApp to ask about places in your child’s grade.
Visit the school — Tour the building, see lessons and meet the admissions team.
Meet and assess — A friendly conversation for future first graders. From Grade 2, a short assessment in mathematics and English.
Submit documents — Bring the documents from the list below to the school office.
Welcome to Indigo West — Sign the agreement, receive the uniform information and get ready for the first day.

## Documents: What to prepare (admissions.html)
Copy of the birth certificate
Copies of both parents’ passports
Medical record (form 026/u) and vaccination card
Personal file and report card from the previous school (for transfers)
3×4 cm photographs, 4 pieces
Application form completed at the school office

## Tuition fees (admissions.html)
Tuition is set for each academic year. Please contact the admissions office for current fees and payment options.

## Which grades do you teach? (admissions.html)
We teach Grades 1–12. Primary school is Grades 1–6; middle and high school, with the Cambridge programme, is Grades 7–12.

## Is the school for boys and girls? (admissions.html)
Yes. Indigo Academy West is a co-educational school: boys and girls study together.

## In which language are primary classes taught? (admissions.html)
Primary classes follow the Russian-language programme, with extra English lessons every week and Kyrgyz language lessons.

## What is the Singapore method? (admissions.html)
A way of teaching, especially mathematics, in which children first work with objects, then with pictures and models, and only then with numbers and symbols. It builds real understanding.

## Are robotics, chess and komuz paid extras? (admissions.html)
No, at Indigo Academy West robotics, chess and komuz are part of the timetable. Please ask the office about any additional clubs.

## Do you have native English-speaking teachers? (admissions.html)
Yes. Native English-speaking teachers are part of our teaching staff.

## Can we visit before applying? (admissions.html)
Yes, and we recommend it. Call us to agree a convenient day and time for a personal tour.
